questions.stem: A young man has recurrent sinopulmonary infections beginning at age 6 months, absent B cells, and very low immunoglobulins of all classes. Which defect is present?
pearls: XLA: BTK; no B cells; recurrent bacterial infections after 6 months.
questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.rationale:
Bruton agammaglobulinemia is X-linked BTK deficiency, preventing pre-B cell maturation. Infections occur after maternal IgG wanes, at 6 months. CD19-positive cells are absent, and lymph nodes and tonsils are small.

Treat with IVIG.

questions.stem: A man is brought in after ingesting antifreeze. He has an elevated anion gap metabolic acidosis, an osmolar gap, and acute kidney injury. Which finding is expected on urine microscopy?
pearls: Anion gap acidosis plus osmolar gap plus oxalate crystals: ethylene glycol.
questions.subject: Pathology
questions.rationale:
Ethylene glycol is metabolized by alcohol dehydrogenase to glycolic and oxalic acids. Oxalate precipitates with calcium in tubules as needle-shaped (monohydrate) or envelope-shaped (dihydrate) crystals, causing tubular obstruction and direct toxic ATN. Treatment: fomepizole (alcohol dehydrogenase inhibitor), hemodialysis, and correction of acidosis.

**Why the others are wrong**
- Cystine crystals: cystinuria.
- Uric acid crystals: acidic urine, tumor lysis, or gout.
- Struvite crystals: alkaline urine from urease-producing bacteria.

questions.stem: A term pregnancy has a nonreactive NST. The remaining four biophysical profile components, including amniotic fluid volume, are normal. What is the biophysical profile score?
pearls: Oligohydramnios is the component most tied to chronic uteroplacental insufficiency; it is an indication for further evaluation or delivery depending on GA.
questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynecology
questions.rationale:
Each normal component earns 2 points. With four normal components (breathing, movement, tone, fluid) and only the NST abnormal (0 points), the total is **8/10**, which is considered reassuring when the amniotic fluid is normal.

The **modified BPP** combines the NST with an amniotic fluid assessment (AFI above 5 cm or deepest pocket ≥2 cm) and is commonly used for antenatal surveillance.
